common_name: Sonoran Desert Organ-Pipe Cactus Fly (Cactophilic Detoxification & Cuticular Epicuticle)

phenomenon_scale.anatomical_structure: Turing pigment stripe / ocellus wavelength in Drosophila mojavensis (2.4 µm, detail scale)

parameters.note: Du and Dv are derived in the script so that argmax_k sigma(k) equals 2*pi/lambda_target_m. They are not copied from slot 2981 (alpha_scale 1.33, beta_offset 0.412, 96 µm).

equations.schnakenberg: du/dt = gamma*(a - u + u^2 v) + Du * lap(u); dv/dt = gamma*(b - u^2 v) + Dv * lap(v)
equations.jacobian: f_u = gamma*(-1 + 2*u0*v0); f_v = gamma*u0^2; g_u = gamma*(-2*u0*v0); g_v = gamma*(-u0^2)
equations.dispersion: sigma(k) = largest real eigenvalue of J - k^2 diag(Du, Dv)
equations.leading_order_kc: k_c^2 = (Dv*f_u + Du*g_v) / (2*Du*Dv)  (Murray form; reported alongside k_star)
equations.chronospecies_square_law: s = (lambda_nm / 2380)^2; Du' = s*Du; Dv' = s*Dv; lambda' = lambda_star * sqrt(s)

wikimedia_habitus.role: real CC/PD taxonomic illustration; too small to be the 480 px fitness target

reported_in_source: Turing 1952 dispersion mechanism and diffusion-driven instability
Matzkin et al. 2006/2012 and Allan & Matzkin 2019: D. mojavensis host shifts among cactus species, with transcriptional and genomic differentiation
Drosophila 12 Genomes Consortium 2007: D. mojavensis genome in the repleta group
reconstructed_in_script: Absolute Du, Dv calibrated so the most-unstable wavelength is the catalog detail length 2.38e-06 m (2.4 µm)
Chronospecies wavelengths 3237 nm (D. miranda) and 1948 nm (D. novamexicana) via lambda proportional to sqrt(D) at fixed Jacobian and R=80
Composite of the saturated activator onto the canonical gallery plate for the animation's last frame
does_not_claim: That 2.38 µm was measured on a D. mojavensis SEM or ocellus in the cited papers
That D. miranda is the phylogenetic ancestor of D. mojavensis (campaign chronoseries order only)
That the gallery plate's printed 100 µm bar is the phenomenon scale of this slot
That DOI 10.1534/genetics.106.059444 is a Matzkin cactus paper
